summary.headline: Triton Valves Q4 FY26 revenue rose to about ₹159 crore (from ₹142 crore YoY), with FY26 adjusted PBT near ₹15.5 crore, roughly double the prior year.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of about ₹159 crore versus ₹142 crore a year earlier and ₹152 crore sequentially, with quarterly PBT (ex-exceptional) of about ₹4.7 crore versus ₹1 crore YoY. EBITDA was eroded by simultaneous rises in copper/zinc and the US dollar, which management said it passes to customers with a one-quarter lag. Climate control remained weak due to Chinese dumping, while metals gained from a second casting line and tube/alloy orders. The NCLT order for the merger of Tritonvalves Climatech into Triton Valves was described as expected within one to two weeks.

from ₹1 crore YoY; marginal improvement QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Commodity/FX cost impact on EBITDA and PBT
financial_highlights.change: management says profit would have been ~₹2 crore higher without one-way movement

segments.name: Automotive (tyre and tube valves, OEM, EV, TPMS, aftermarket)
segments.commentary: FY26 standalone sales about ₹434 crore before intercompany elimination. Management claims 60-65% market share overall and about 90%+ in tubeless valves; TPMS valve deal with AUMOVIO (ex-Continental Automotive) to enter serial production by end-2026.

segments.name: Metals (Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: FY26 standalone sales about ₹383 crore before elimination. Second casting line commissioned; tube order book above 50 tons/month, targeted near 100 tons/month. FY27 volume target above 7,000 tons, with brass realisations of ₹950-1,000/kg versus ~₹600/kg a year earlier.

segments.name: Climate control (Tritonvalves Climatech)
segments.commentary: FY26 standalone sales about ₹17 crore. Under pressure from Chinese dumping (management cites ~₹800 crore of imports); Mitsubishi Electric mass production started in Chennai; US export of connectors begins Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth of 10-12% across tyre/tube, OEM, EV and metals verticals, with metals volumes of 15-25% in internal plan; climate control excluded as a question mark pending government action.
Margin in FY27 expected to be significantly better (management cites double-digit improvement) in rupees per kg, though EBITDA percentage may look optically lower; no numeric margin guidance given.
Top-line growth of 15-25% expected in FY27, largely commodity-driven; management asks investors to focus on constant-price volume growth.
Management targets crossing ₹1,000 crore revenue by FY29-FY30, possibly earlier if commodity inflation persists.
Merger tax benefit estimated at ₹6-7 crore cash tax shield, which would remove advance tax payments for a year or two, subject to assessment.
Capex of about ₹15-20 crore over the next two to three years; existing infrastructure can reach ~₹1,000 crore revenue with that capex.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation above 75-85% in some automotive lines; capacity additions planned, mainly on automotive side, with CWIP tied to equipment yet to be commissioned.
Second brass casting line in metals fully commissioned and running at full production as of Q4 FY26.
Special express feeder power line from substation to plant expected to complete in Q1 FY27.
No further fundraise planned in FY27 beyond the earlier preferential allotment; capex to be funded from internal accruals/borrowings.
demand_pricing: Brass prices have risen about 50% YoY, from ₹600/kg to ₹950-1,000/kg; copper near $14,000/t and USD/INR about 95 per management.
Quarterly commodity indexation with automotive customers creates a one-quarter pass-through lag; oil-derived inputs (butyl rubber, EPDM, carbon black, process oil) also up.
Metals order book described as very large; new tube products and special alloys for a European customer, first Chinese brass ingot order and a Middle East defence order.
Climate control hit by air-conditioner sector slowdown and Chinese dumping via Vietnam and Thailand; company lobbying DPIIT/Commerce Ministry for QCO and MIP.
Receivables rising broadly in line with sales; some elongation from tyre industry, not vehicle OEMs. Normalised working capital cycle about 55-60 days (metals much shorter).

qa_highlights.question: What brass volume and margin profile should be expected for FY27 with the second line running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets over 7,000 tons in FY27 and says margin per kg will be significantly better, with double-digit improvement, but declined to give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the P&L become less sensitive to raw-material spikes compared with 12 quarters ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits the natural hedge between Triton Valves (automotive) and Future Tech (metals), plus different contracting methods, and says the structure is better now, though a sudden dollar move would still hit.

qa_highlights.question: What are the benefits of the amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated cash tax benefit of about ₹6 crore (subject to assessment), elimination of intercompany rent and interest, and headcount and operating efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and capacity outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth of 15-25% is mostly commodity-driven; management prefers constant-price volume growth and expects ₹1,000 crore revenue by FY29-FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market size and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Automotive domestic addressable market about ₹800-1,000 crore; climate control about ₹1,000 crore; brass mill TAM described as a few billion dollars. Market share 60-65% in automotive, 90%+ in tubeless valves, 85-90% in some EV components.

qa_highlights.question: Is TPMS mandatory and are there aerospace or defence programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: TPMS is not yet mandatory; management expects it may become so. Defence programmes in India, the Middle East and the US are at an early stage.

risks_watch: Copper, zinc and USD/INR moving one way; management says the lag costs about ₹1.75 crore of FY26 EBITDA and could worsen if costs keep rising in Q1 FY27.
Climate control: continued Chinese dumping; outcome of QCO and MIP lobbying is uncertain and management declined to forecast the segment.
Receivables build-up with Q4 sales rising; collection improvement is only partly in management's control.
Merger completion (NCLT order expected within weeks) and realisation of the ₹6-7 crore tax benefit subject to assessment.
Middle East crisis effects on raw material supply and orders; management says the war briefly paused one order.
summary.management_tone: Confident on automotive and metals volumes and structural hedging, but cautious on margins and climate control, where management repeatedly declined to give numeric guidance. Management openly said profitability was below its aspirations and that it is tempering growth to limit debt risk.

growth.why: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-25% (midpoint 20%), largely commodity-driven, with 10-12% volume growth across auto and metals; backed by the commissioned second brass line, a metals order book above 50 t/month targeting ~100 t/month, and ₹15-20 cr capex, but no numeric margin or climate control guidance.
